messages.author: 87cf4991b6a810ee
messages.subject: Why no position_overlap() for geom_bar?
parts:
Why is there no such thing as position_overlap() for bar charts?
position_dodge() wastes too much space. I want to make a bar chart
where the bars overlap and are rendered with the tallest bar in back
and the shortest bar in front.

--
Ryan Hope, M.S.
CogWorks Lab
Cognitive Science Department
Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute

messages.subject: Re: Why no position_overlap() for geom_bar?
parts:
Simple example:

ggplot(data.frame(x=rep(c("A","B"),each=3),y=rep(c("X","Y","Z"),times=2),z=c(1,2,3,2,3,1)))
+ geom_bar(aes(x=x,y=z,fill=y),position="dodge")

ggplot(data.frame(x=rep(c("A","B"),each=3),y=rep(c("X","Y","Z"),times=2),z=c(1,2,3,2,3,1)))
+ geom_bar(aes(x=x,y=z,fill=y),position="identity")

In the second example much of the data is hidden.

messages.subject: Re: Why no position_overlap() for geom_bar?
parts: Give them an alpha and they'll all show up. The issue is if your factor levels are always in the same order of quantity or not. If they are, you can easily do this, if they aren't... messages.subject: Re: Why no position_overlap() for geom_bar?
parts:
Alpha is not a good enough solution because then the key does not make
sense. I know I can't reorder a factor for each bar, hence the
problem. There needs to be some built in way to make overlapping bar
charts work better. The current implementation is stupid. What
possible benefit is there to having overlapping bars if they are just
going to hide data?

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Why no position_overlap() for geom_bar?
parts:
Ryan, 
What is it you are trying to visualize? Is a stacked bar chart that alternates the order of the bars really going to easily show your reader what you want them to see, without issues of mis-interpretation? From my perspective, even if you could do what you want, it seems like the position="dodge" plot is much better for comparison within each x-axis value than your current ideal could. Just my opinion though.

Brandon

messages.author: fd4f3538f907404b
messages.subject: Re: Why no position_overlap() for geom_bar?
parts:
I wouldn't try to insist that the OP plot things in any particular
way, *but* I would have the following thoughts/suggestions, which
parallel lots of advice given in stat-graphics fora over the years:

* try a dot plot (geom_point()) rather than a bar plot: this will
naturally solve the overlapping problem you have. For a percent
composition score, it might also make sense to use stacked bars ...
although I see that these percentages don't add up to 1 ...
* use coord_flip() to turn the graph sideways so that labels can be
read more easily, without needing additional rotation (you also get more
usable room on a standard portrait-layout page)
* unless people really need to use the graph to look up the values of
_specific_ hops variety, consider sorting them in some way more
meaningful than alphabetically [oh, OK, I see you have a "sort by"
button ...]
* consider using scale_colour_brewer() to get dichromat-friendly colours

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Why no position_overlap() for geom_bar?
parts:
The "stupid" current implementation isn't designed to make the bar graphs that you have in mind. All position="identity" does is tell ggplot to leave the geoms in place, without any modification. Each color-set of bars is added as a layer to the plot, and the blue ones happen to be on the top layer in your example.

The question of "what possible benefit is there to having overlapping bars" isn't the driving issue behind position="identity". The identity position adjustment can be used for any geom, not just bars, and it is indeed used as the default for many geoms.


Regarding your desired output: the kind of graph you're asking for would look just like a stacked bar plot (though possibly with an inconsistent stacking order, depending on the data) and could easily be confused for one. I don't think I've seen any examples of overlaid bars where the layering order depends on the bar height.

You could have each group with different widths, although it's potentially misleading since the areas aren't quite proportional to the value:

dat <- data.frame(
  x=rep(c("A","B"),each=3),
  y=c(1,2,3,2,3,1),
  z=rep(c("X","Y","Z"),times=2))

dat$width <- .9
dat$width[dat$z=="Y"] <- .75
dat$width[dat$z=="Z"] <- .6

ggplot(dat, aes(x=x,y=y,fill=z, width=width)) +
  geom_bar(position="identity", stat="identity", colour="black")


A good alternative is a Cleveland-style dot plot, as Ben suggested.

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: Why no position_overlap() for geom_bar?
parts:
Ryan,

You can achieve what you want by adding the data on separate geom_bar calls:

ggplot('the data you want at the back', aes(x=x,y=z,fill=y)) #note that aes is the same for all the calls
+ geom_bar(position="identity") 
+ geom_bar(data= 'the variable you want in the front', position="identity") 

Still, a position_overlap would be much better.
I hope this helps.
LLP

I have nearly 80 factors on the x-axis and with 3 fill factors, thats
